coordinates.note: No rank<=7 source fetched this session (the SAGE 1999 results paper's abstract does not state coordinates; the official Baksan/INR site returned 404) gives numeric coordinates for the underground lab specifically. Per A17/A23, recorded as `kind: campus`/`confidence: approximate` off Wikipedia (rank 12) rather than as a fabricated `underground_lab`-precision point.

depth.note: Wikipedia (rank 12) is the only source found for a 2100 m figure. The SAGE 1999 results paper (arXiv:astro-ph/9907113) gives the overburden of the SAGE laboratory as 4700 meters of water equivalent (see depth_mwe), not a vertical depth in metres.
depth.quote: stored 2,100 m (6,900 ft) underground at the Baksan Neutrino Observatory in the Caucasus Mountains in Russia

depth_mwe.note: Overhead shielding of the SAGE gallium laboratory, 3.5 km from the entrance of the horizontal adit into Mount Andyrchi (SAGE 1999 results paper).
depth_mwe.quote: has an overhead shielding of 4700 meters of water equivalent

summary.plain: A chamber more than two kilometres inside a mountain in the Russian Caucasus, holding tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch solar neutrinos.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory of the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, ~2100 m (6900 ft) underground in the Caucasus Mountains, Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia, housing the SAGE gallium detector.
